# Best 18650 chargers

**Best overall: XTAR VC4SL (~$33)**
- It has 4 independent bays, USB-C with QC3.0 input, and adjustable current from 0.25A to 3A.
- The screen shows voltage, current, capacity and internal resistance per cell. It also has capacity-test and storage modes, and fits protected 21700s.
- Best-Batteries rates it 4.3/5 and lists it at $32.90 ([review and price](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/)). VoltRated also recommends it for 18650/21700 users ([guide](https://voltrated.com/guides/best-chargers)).
- Caveats from [Stephen Knight's review](https://www.stephenknightphotography.com/post/charger-review-xtar-vc4sl): it defaults to the highest current, so drop it to 1A or less for 18650s. It can mistake NiMH cells for Li-ion, and it doesn't charge LiFePO4. You need a QC3.0 adapter for full speed.

**Best for fast charging or LiFePO4: Nitecore UMS4 (~$39)**
- It does up to 3A in one slot and supports LiFePO4. It has an LCD, shows battery health via internal resistance, and has reverse-polarity and short-circuit protection.
- Specs: [Nitecore's page](https://www.nitecore.com/mobile-product/ums4). Price: [Best-Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/), which lists it at $38.95.

**Best budget: Tenergy TN270 ($18.99)**
- It's a simple 2-bay wall charger with reverse-polarity detection and a 12-month warranty.
- It charges at only 500 mA per slot, so a 3,000 mAh cell takes about 6–7 hours. It has no USB input and no LCD.
- [Buy from Tenergy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn270-li-ion-18650-charger). This is an affiliate link.

**Other options (from a single review site)**
- The [Smashing Robotics roundup](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/) picks the Keenstone 4-bay (500 mA or 1 A per slot, wide chemistry support) as its top choice. It also picks the IMREN 2-bay USB-C as a pocket-sized travel option.
- That page is full of Amazon affiliate links, and I only saw part of it, so treat those picks with more caution. I don't have a direct purchase link for either.

**What to look for:** Independent bays rather than paired ones, a proper CC/CV cutoff at 4.2V, and a charge current you can lower. Gentler charging (about 0.5C) is better for cell life ([VoltRated](https://voltrated.com/guides/best-chargers)). Avoid no-name units that don't say how they decide a cell is full.

I couldn't verify live prices or find direct retailer links for the XTAR and Nitecore, so check the current price before you buy.
